newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian ANZ job ads fall 2.3 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian ANZ job ads fall 2.3 pct in August.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) said on Monday its job advertisement series fell by a seasonally adjusted 2.3 percent in August to their lowest level since March 1994.
The series fell 4.2 percent in July and was down 14.4 percent on its level in August 1995.
In trend terms, job ads were down 0.8 percent in August, after a 1.4 percent fall in July, to be 12.6 percent down on the year.
"August's results indicate that demand for labour remains soft," ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said in a statement.
The August result was consistent with trend growth in employment of about 7,000 per month over the next six months, a little less than indicated earlier in the year, ANZ said.

"However, since growth in the labour force has also slowed quite markedly this year (from over 20,000 per month in mid-1995 to less than 5,000 per month over the past three months) this may be sufficient to prevent a marked increase in measured unemployment over the remainder of 1996," Eslake said.
Unemployment was 8.5 percent in July and official August labour force data are due on Thursday.

Job ads were down in all states expect Tasmania and Western Australia. South Australia posted a 9.3 percent fall in job ads, while ads fell 3.7 percent in New South Wales, 2.3 percent in Queensland and 1.1 percent in Victoria.

The ANZ said research suggested the job ads series led official employment data by about six months, with annual growth in the series typically "explaining" about two-thirds of the annual growth rate in the official employment statistics.

The ANZ said these conclusions had been challenged in a study recently published by the Commonwealth Treasury, which suggested the level of job ads rather than the rate of change may be the statistically more important leading indicator of employment.
The ANZ said it was reviewing the issue.
